{{Quote|Just like shootin' womp rats, eh kid?|Unknown [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] [[Soldier/Legends|soldier]]|<ref name="BattlefrontII">''[[Star Wars: Battlefront II]]''</ref>}}
'''Womp rats''' were large, omnivorous rodents native to [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], widely considered to be pests. They were slightly larger than two [[Meter/Legends|meters]] in size. There were three species of womp rats: ones that lived in [[Beggar's Canyon/Legends|Beggar's Canyon]], ones that lived in the [[Jundland Wastes/Legends|Jundland Wastes]], and [[swamp womp rat]]s. It was not unheard of for people to have domesticated womp rats as pets, but [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] and his friends used to "bulls-eye" womp rats while flying [[T-16 skyhopper/Legends|T-16 skyhoppers]], for fun and target practice.

==Biology and appearance==
[[File:Womp_rat_AA.jpg|thumb|left|180px|Jundland Waste womp rats]]
{{Quote|I used to bull's-eye womp rats in my T-16 back home. They're not much bigger than two meters.|Luke Skywalker|<ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}</ref>}}
While womp rats were opportunists and fond of carrion and refuse, they were also predators, though most of their prey were old, sick, or generally weak. Their normal prey included smaller animals, such as [[Profogg/Legends|profoggs]] and [[Scurrier/Legends|scurriers]]. Womp rats traveled in packs to overwhelm larger prey items, such as [[Dewback/Legends|dewbacks]] and [[Bantha/Legends|banthas]]. These packs consisted of up to 20 individuals.<ref name="WSW">''[[The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide]]''</ref> When they bite, their teeth set in and the animals will not release their hold, even if they are killed; [[Owen Lars/Legends|Owen Lars]] had seen a [[Bantha/Legends|bantha]] with a desiccated womp rat skull still biting down on it.

Womp rats often nested in landfill sites.<ref name="WSW" />

With lengths of up to 3 [[Meter/Legends|meters]],<ref name="SW9">[[Star Wars (1977) 9|''Star Wars'' (1977) 9]]</ref> womp rats were vicious, mean mammals, and were often used for target practice. Some womp rats on Tatooine were prone to [[Gray Rot]].<ref name="Star Wars Galaxies: An Empire Divided">{{GalaxiesAED}}</ref>

Womp rats were a menace to any permanent settlement. They reproduced at a staggering rate and were known to stalk urban alleyways and remote [[Moisture farm/Legends|moisture farms]] alike, prompting some authorities to put a bounty on the creatures. When found in the desert, womp rats also hunted in packs, emerging from burrows and swarming their unfortunate victims.<ref name="Womp Rat Swtor">{{TORcite|type=codex|Womp Rat}}</ref>

Womp rats were also very fast and stealthy. They could have had the ability to cloak themselves with [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] since [[Ki-Adi-Mundi/Legends|Ki-Adi-Mundi]] and [[Aurra Sing/Legends|Aurra Sing]] both found out that they could barely sense them with the Force aiding them.

[[File:Womp_rat_btm.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Beggar's Canyon womp rats]]

Easy targets were sometimes called "sitting womp-rats".<ref name="SW9" />

Given its repugnant bestial qualities, it therefore may be somewhat surprising for some to learn that a popular flavor of soup on Tatooine was "[[Cream of womprat/Legends|Cream of Womprat soup]]," often prepared by [[Beru Whitesun Lars/Legends|Beru Whitesun Lars]].<ref name="ANHrev">{{CCG|set=A New Hope Limited|cardname=Luke's Hunting Rifle}}</ref>

The [[Jundland Wastes/Legends|Jundland Wastes]] womp rat appeared shortly after Imperials arrived on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], and some have speculated it was a mutated form of the Beggar's Canyon womp rat, affected by chemicals from Imperial waste dumps. Some of its mutations include a larger size, slower reproduction rate, and lower numbers than Beggar's Canyon womp rat. Their ears are also elongated and winglike.

Another variety, the [[swamp womp rat]], was found on a few fringe worlds as well as on [[Cularin/Legends|Cularin]].<ref name="Creature Feature: Swamp Womp Rat!">{{Wizards|url=starwars/article.asp?x=sw20010315b&c=rpg|series=Creature Feature|text=Swamp Womp Rat!}}</ref>

The [[Grunge fever]] disease was known to be spread by womp rats.<ref name="SWG:ACO">{{SWGcite|exp=NGE|type=class|Legacy|Animal Control Officer|Tatooine}}</ref>

==History==
Around the time of the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]], some of the larger womp rats were domesticated and used as mounts.<ref name="Cartel Market">[[Cartel Market|''Star Wars: The Old Republic'' Cartel Market]]</ref>

In [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], as he led the [[Ghostling]] children to freedom through [[Mos Espa/Legends|Mos Espa's]] subterranean sand drains, young [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] was attacked by a womp rat. Anakin knew its unmistakable growl from his time working in [[Watto]] the [[Toydarian/Legends|Toydarian's]] junkyard, knew that the foul creature could grow to be as big as a man and could carry off children and full-grown [[Jawa/Legends|Jawas]]. But by using the same [[Beamdrill/Legends|beamdrill]] that he employed to break his friends [[Kitster Chanchani Banai|Kitster]], [[Pala Kwi'teksa|Pala]], [[Dorn (Bothan)|Dorn]] and the [[Ghostling]]s out of their [[Mos Espa Grand Arena/Legends|Mos Espa Grand Arena]] cells (as they awaited their execution by [[Gardulla Besadii the Elder/Legends|Gardulla the Hutt]]), the fledgling hero was able to overpower the vermin. By setting the tool's plasma beam for a long, narrow ray, the beamdrill shot forth a searing white stream of superheated gas like a flamethrower, slicing the womp rat in two.<ref>[[Tatooine/Legends|''Episode I Adventures 8: Trouble on Tatooine'']]</ref>

During the [[Battle of Gall (Clone Wars)|Battle of Gall]] in the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], Skywalker recalled how womp rats escape predators by burrowing into the sand and used his [[Anakin Skywalker's second lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] to cutting into the floor of the [[Shielded Separatist craft]], which his [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Ahsoka Tano/Legends|Ahsoka Tano]] soon follow him in before the pair landed in their [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]] as the craft exploded from above.<ref name="Inside Job">{{TCWComicCite|6.1|Inside Job}}</ref>

The Beggar's Canyon womp rat reproduced at an alarming rate. Once it reproduced to such a point that the population could not be kept in check, and womp rats were hunting [[Jawa/Legends|Jawas]] and raiding storehouses. The [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Prefect/Legends|prefect]] of Tatooine and the Affiliated Moisture Farmers then passed a bounty ordinance of ten [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] per rat. [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] and his friend [[Biggs Darklighter/Legends|Biggs Darklighter]] got enough womp rats to upgrade their T-16 skyhoppers and have enough money for the [[Imperial Academy/Legends|Academy]].

Shortly before the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], when another [[Rebel Alliance/Legends|Rebel]] pilot protested during [[General/Legends|General]] [[Jan Dodonna/Legends|Dodonna]]'s attack plan briefing in the [[Great Temple/Legends|Great Temple]] that the two-[[meter]] target on the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]] was impossible to hit even for a [[computer/Legends|computer]], Skywalker countered that he used to "bulls-eye" womp rats that were not much bigger than two meters.<ref name="StarWarsNovelization">[[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope'' novelization]]</ref><ref name="ANH" />

After the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], Animal Control [[Officer/Legends|officer]] [[Entha Kandela]] tasked a spacer to eliminate womp rats around [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]] to prevent propagation of grunge fever in the city.<ref name="SWG:ACO" />

==Behind the scenes==
Womp rats were first mentioned in the 1976 [[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|novelization]] of ''[[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope]]'',<ref name="StarWarsNovelization"></ref> before being mentioned in the film, which was released in 1977.<ref name="ANH" />

The [[Mutant Womprat]] appears in the game ''[[Super Star Wars]]'' as boss of Level 6: Land of the Banthas, fought by [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]]. The creature was accompanied by several smaller Womp Rats.<ref name="Super Star Wars">''[[Super Star Wars]]''</ref>

In the [[2001]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron II: Rogue Leader]]'', the player must play a minigame in the training session where they strafe womp rats.<ref name="Star Wars: Rogue Squadron II: Rogue Leader">''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron II: Rogue Leader]]''</ref>
